headline_marked: [[OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra]], claiming it's 'most intelligent and aligned model in the world'
headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra, claiming it's 'most intelligent and aligned model in the world'
summary: GPT-6 Astra excels at complex multi-step tasks across software engineering, cybersecurity, and general professional work. It's rolling out today to select organizations and will soon be available to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users.
details: OpenAI has launched GPT-6 Astra, its new frontier model, claiming it is "the most intelligent and aligned model in the world." This release comes after a brief slowdown in frontier model development.

Astra excels at agentic computer-use tasks, including browsing, software engineering, cybersecurity, and general professional work. A demo shows it handling multiple tasks simultaneously, from 3D modeling to coding, with strong visual judgment.

The model achieved a 98.6% score on ARC-AGI-3, a benchmark for solving unfamiliar problems, though benchmark configurations can vary. It also scored 57.7% on Terminal Bench 4.0 for coding and 59.3% on Agent's Last Exam for agentic capabilities, significantly outperforming GPT-5.6 Sol.

Astra demonstrated exceptional cybersecurity skills, achieving a perfect score on ExploitBench and solving 88.0% of SRE-Bench tasks in a single attempt. OpenAI states that improved alignment and stronger protections are built in to withstand jailbreak requests and monitor misuse.

GPT-6 Astra is rolling out today to a limited set of organizations and will soon be available to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users. It will also be accessible through the OpenAI API, costing $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.

While token costs are on the higher end, OpenAI President Greg Brockman emphasizes that "price per task" is a more relevant metric for businesses. The company promises Astra can efficiently complete a wide variety of tasks for an appropriate cost and speed.

headline_marked: [[Xbox Cloud Gaming gets new time limits]] for Game Pass subscribers starting in November
headline: Xbox Cloud Gaming gets new time limits for Game Pass subscribers starting in November
summary: Starting in November, Game Pass subscribers will face new monthly limits on streaming time, with a pay-as-you-go option for additional use. This change impacts an estimated 1.2 million users.
details: Microsoft is introducing new monthly time limits for its Xbox Cloud Gaming service, starting in November. This change impacts Game Pass Ultimate subscribers who previously enjoyed unlimited access since 2020.

The company states this change will affect approximately 4% of Game Pass subscribers, an estimated 1.2 million users out of 30 million. These heavy streamers will now incur higher costs for their usage.

Subscribers who exceed their monthly streaming allotment will be able to purchase additional time, though specific pricing and availability have not yet been shared. Players without Game Pass can also buy timed access to stream eligible games they own.

Microsoft attributes the new limits to the rising cost of providing cloud gaming, which increases as more people use the service and play for longer durations. Unlike linear video streaming, cloud gaming demands significant computing resources on remote servers.

This announcement follows a period where Microsoft's cloud-focused vision has seen competitors like Google Stadia shut down and Amazon Luna scale back. Microsoft itself noted in 2023 that cloud gaming "makes up only a tiny fraction of the billions of hours of gameplay each year."
